Publish a source release: features, profiles, horizons, observations

Source: R/publish-source.R
soil_publish_source.Rd

Admits a provider dataset release into the hub as new canonical geography and original observations: builds a provider-neutral source bundle (one NDJSON record per feature, profile, component, horizon and observation), uploads it with its manifest and SHA-256 checksum, has the API validate it and promotes it as an immutable release. New geography never goes through the publication of derived values (soil_publish_values()).

Usage

soil_publish_source(
  soil = soil_session(),
  manifest,
  features,
  profiles = NULL,
  components = NULL,
  horizons = NULL,
  observations = NULL,
  idempotency_key,
  auto_promote = FALSE,
  wait = TRUE,
  keep_file = FALSE,
  timeout = 3600,
  poll = 5,
  progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

soil

A session; the default session when omitted. Client-side: not sent to the API.

manifest

A named list describing the release: provider_code, provider_name, dataset_code, dataset_name, release_code, support_type ("observed_point_profile", "polygon_estimate", "map_unit_profile_relation", "non_spatial_profile", "non_spatial_estimate"), default_geometry_kind ("POINT", "POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON", "NONE"), and optionally provider_website_url, dataset_description, source_url, release_checksum_sha256, licence_text, citation_text, source_table_prefix and assets (a data frame or list of records with asset_role, source_url, checksum_sha256, media_type, byte_size). Property mappings are not part of the manifest: the API resolves them from its own mappings of the provider. API form field manifest (JSON text).

features

The features of the release, each with a source_record_id column: an sf object (needs the package sf), or the path of a spatial file – a GeoJSON file (.geojson, .json) is read without sf when in WGS84, any other format is read with sf::st_read(). The other columns travel as attributes of the feature record (source_support, ...). For a non-spatial dataset (default_geometry_kind = "NONE"), a plain data frame. Records of the NDJSON bundle sent as API form field file.

profiles, components, horizons, observations

Optional data frames (or lists of records) of the other record types, each with its source_record_id and the source_record_id of its parent (feature_source_id, profile_source_id, component_source_id, horizon_source_id). Horizons carry top_depth_cm, bottom_depth_cm, horizon_name; components component_rank, proportion_percent; observations property_code, value, unit, status, and optionally method and quality. NA fields are left out (an observation needs its unit declared). Records of the NDJSON bundle sent as API form field file.

idempotency_key

Key of this ingest (at most 200 characters), stable for one bundle. API form field idempotency_key.

auto_promote

Let the server validate and promote the job (TRUE), or validate and promote from the client (FALSE). API form field auto_promote.

wait

Validate, promote and wait for the end of the job; FALSE returns after the upload. Client-side: not sent to the API.

keep_file

Keep the NDJSON bundle written for the upload: its path is in file (a temporary file, removed when the R session ends; copy it to keep it longer). By default it is deleted. Client-side: not sent to the API.

timeout, poll

Seconds to wait for the job, and between two polls. Client-side: not sent to the API.

progress

Print the progress of the job. Client-side: not sent to the API.

Value

A soil_source_ingest list: job_id, status, provider_code, dataset_code, release_code, auto_promote, record_count (records sent), record_counts (sent, by record type), staged_counts (staged by the API, by record type), published_count, release_id, receipt_id, validation (a soil_source_validation, or NULL), unmapped_property_codes, job (the last soil_job), checksum_sha256, byte_size and file (the bundle path with keep_file = TRUE, else NULL).

Details

Before any request the client checks, and lists by record in the errors of a soilhub_argument_error:

  • the manifest (required fields, codes of lowercase letters, digits and _, support_type, default_geometry_kind, checksums, assets);

  • every record has a source_record_id, unique within its record type (text, or whole numbers turned into text);

  • every profile, component, horizon and observation names an existing parent (feature_source_id, profile_source_id, component_source_id, horizon_source_id);

  • every observation has property_code, a unit declaration and a status "observed" or "computed";

  • features have a CRS (an sf object without one is refused; any other CRS is transformed to WGS84, EPSG:4326, the only CRS of the API) and POINT, POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON geometries, neither empty nor with missing coordinates.

Steps, with wait = TRUE:

  1. upload (POST /source-ingests, never repeated automatically, no total timeout); the API records the checksum of the file received, compared with the checksum of the file sent;

  2. with auto_promote = FALSE (default) the client validates (POST /source-ingests/{job_id}/validate): an invalid bundle is a soilhub_validation_error whose errors lists the rejected records (record_number in the bundle, record_type, row of its table) and the job fails; the counts staged by the API, per record type and in all, must equal the records sent, else a soilhub_api_error (code staged_count_mismatch) and nothing is promoted; then it promotes (POST /source-ingests/{job_id}/promote);

  3. with auto_promote = TRUE the server's ingest worker validates and promotes the job, and the client waits for it (soil_job_wait()); a failed job is a soilhub_job_error with the rejected records in errors;

  4. the published counts are reconciled with the records sent (a difference is a soilhub_reconciliation_warning).

Property codes that the API cannot map to a variable of the hub are a soilhub_unmapped_properties_warning: their observations are stored with the original code and do not appear under a canonical variable until a mapping exists (see soil_variable_mappings()).

With wait = FALSE the function returns after the upload: follow the job with soil_source_validate() and soil_source_promote() (or soil_job_wait() when auto_promote = TRUE). The API keeps no list of a user's jobs: keep the job_id.

The same idempotency_key with the same file returns the job already submitted (a completed job is returned as it is, an ended one is a soilhub_job_error); the same key with another file is a soilhub_conflict_error (HTTP 409): use a new key. Releases are immutable: a release_code already promoted for the dataset makes the promotion fail.

Rights: soil:publish. Capability: source_ingest.

See also

soil_source_validate(), soil_source_promote(), soil_job()

Other writing: soil_product(), soil_product_version(), soil_publish_health(), soil_publish_values(), soil_register_variable(), soil_run_open(), soil_source_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(sf)
sites <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(source_record_id = c("P1", "P2"), x = c(500100, 501200), y = c(4520300, 4521900)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32633
)
manifest <- list(
  provider_code = "unina", provider_name = "University of Naples Federico II",
  dataset_code = "campania_profiles", dataset_name = "Campania soil profiles",
  release_code = "2026-10", support_type = "observed_point_profile",
  default_geometry_kind = "POINT", licence_text = "CC-BY 4.0"
)
profiles <- data.frame(source_record_id = c("P1", "P2"), feature_source_id = c("P1", "P2"))
components <- data.frame(source_record_id = c("P1", "P2"), profile_source_id = c("P1", "P2"))
horizons <- data.frame(
  source_record_id = c("P1-1", "P2-1"), component_source_id = c("P1", "P2"),
  top_depth_cm = 0, bottom_depth_cm = 30
)
observations <- data.frame(
  source_record_id = c("P1-1-orgc", "P2-1-orgc"), horizon_source_id = c("P1-1", "P2-1"),
  property_code = "orgc", value = c(12.1, 8.4), unit = "g/kg", status = "observed"
)
ingest <- soil_publish_source(
  soil, manifest, sites, profiles, components, horizons, observations,
  idempotency_key = "campania-2026-10"
)
ingest$release_id
} # }
